Graceful shutdown only stops accepting/keeping connections alive; it does not cancel an active HTTP/1 response future. Tokio runtime shutdown is the mechanism that drops outstanding tasks and their I/O resources.

**Boundary:** `ctrl_c()` resolves the shutdown future; hyper marks HTTP/1 connections non-keep-alive, but an active long-poll response remains in the connection/task state machine. Hyper therefore waits for the response body/service future to finish before `Connection::poll` can reach close and `poll_shutdown`. Tokio does not force-cancel ordinary spawned tasks merely because an application-level graceful-shutdown future resolved. The long-poll is interrupted only when the owning task is explicitly aborted/dropped or when runtime shutdown drops outstanding tasks and their I/O resources.
